reason: This passage (Judges 9) depicts God bringing judgment and justice upon specific wrongdoers - Abimelech and the men of Shechem - for their evil deeds (fratricide, conspiracy, and violence), not antagonism toward the Hebrew people generally. God's role is framed as retributive justice: sending division to corrupt parties and ultimately causing the curse of Jotham to fall upon those responsible for the killing of the seventy brothers. The text explicitly states 'So God repaid the evil of Abimelech... and God also made all the evil of the men of Shechem come back upon their heads' - presenting this as divine justice, not antagonism. The narrative distinguishes between punishment of the wicked and the broader Hebrew people.
